title: The Real Alert
intro: A text from your bank. After today, you might be ready to call everything a scam.
But some messages are real. Mirage loves it when you stop trusting the honest ones.

notify.text: We paused a card payment of £212.00…

screen.context: You did not make this payment.

msg.text: paused a card payment of £212.00 at Gadgetz Direct
open the Orrin app to review it
call the number on your statement
We will never ask for your PIN, password or codes.

paused.label: Names the payment
paused.lens: It names the shop and the amount, and says the payment was paused, not made.
paused.why: Specific facts fit a real alert. Scammers can guess some, so you still check through the app.

app.label: Open the app yourself
app.lens: It sends you to the app you already have.
app.why: Pointing you to the app, not to a link, is what honest banks do.

call.label: Number on your statement
call.lens: It tells you to call the number on your statement.
call.why: Using a number you already trust avoids fake numbers.

never.label: Safety reminder
never.lens: It repeats that the bank never asks for your PIN or codes.
never.why: Real banks warn you about scams.

sender.label: Sender name
sender.why: A name alone proves nothing. What the message asks you to do is the real clue: nothing secret, no link.

actions.label: Open the Orrin app myself and review the payment

go_ahead.line: The app showed a payment you did not make, already paused. One tap to confirm it was fraud, and the bank sent a new card.

ignore.line: Nothing bad happened this time. But a real alert deserves a look in your own app.

block_report.line: That was a real alert. When every message looks like a scam, the real warnings get lost too.
block_report.mirageSays: If you trust nothing, I win anyway.

what_if.block_report: Nothing in it asked for money, codes, a PIN or a link. That calm is what real messages look like.
what_if.ignore: Opening your own app is safe, and it tells you whether the payment really was yours.

golden_rule: Real alerts ask for nothing secret and send you to your own app. Check there, never through the text.

quick_check.q: What showed this bank text was genuine?

options.text: It asked for nothing secret and sent you to your own app or the number on your statement
It had a capital letter at the start

quick_check.explain: Names, times and logos can all be copied. Asking for nothing secret, and no link, is the real sign.

hints.nudge: What is this text actually asking you to do?

rows.k: Same thread as your past bank texts
Does the bank ask for your PIN or codes?

rows.v: Open the app or call the number on your statement
